findings.title: No retry on 401 removes the cookie re-read after AccountProvider clears a stale Bearer/impersonation token
findings.body:
The engine authenticates with the Bearer token alone when one is sent (`engine/api/src/platform/auth/platform-auth.service.ts` `resolveActorFromRequestToken`). It reads cookies only when no token is present. The axios interceptor in `console/hooks/usePlatformApi.ts` sends `impersonationToken ?? jwt` from localStorage, and it reads them on every request. On a 401, `AccountProvider` (`console/contexts/account-context.tsx:51-58`) calls `unsetToken()` and `unsetImpersonationToken()` but does not call `mutate()`. Before this change, SWR's default error retry ran `GET /account` again a few seconds later without the Bearer header. A valid BetterAuth cookie then returned 200. `shouldRetryOnError: (error) => error.status !== 401` removes that re-read.

The realistic trigger is an impersonation token: nothing in the console calls `setToken('jwt')`. `Detail.tsx:165` and `JobsManagement.tsx:88` store the token, and its TTL comes from the engine. The console does not set it. An operator who left an impersonation running until the token expired, and who has a valid cookie session, opens a public `resolveAccount` page (`/offers/...`, `/start`, `/agreements/*`). The first `/account` returns 401 and the token is cleared. Nothing reads the account again until a focus, reconnect or reload, so `OfferSiteHeader` shows "Log in" and the Start and agreement pages show the visitor state. `AgreementLinkPage` also reads its link with `revalidateOnFocus: false` after the account settles, so it keeps the signed-out view of the link even after a focus. Private routes are not affected because `RouteAuthBoundary` redirects on the first 401. Only internal operators are affected, and a focus or the "Log in" click recovers, so this is minor.
findings.fix: In the 401 branch of the `AccountProvider` effect, check `getToken()` before clearing. If a token was present, call `mutate()` once after `unsetToken()`/`unsetImpersonationToken()`, so the cookie-only read still happens. Keep the no-retry rule for a visitor who sent no token.
